[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Secure SDLC and DevSecOps Integration Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integrating security into the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and transitioning to a DevSecOps model ensures that security is a shared responsibility throughout the entire application delivery pipeline. This tutorial covers the foundational steps, tools, and automation techniques required to build a secure software supply chain."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 1: Planning and Threat Modeling"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before writing code, security requirements must be defined, and architectural designs must be threat modeled. Threat modeling helps identify potential attack vectors, asset boundaries, and high-risk components early in the design phase."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define security requirements alongside functional requirements in user stories."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perform data flow diagrams and STRIDE-based threat modeling sessions."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 2: Secure Coding and Static Application Security Testing (SAST)"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"As developers write code, IDE plugins and pre-commit hooks catch common vulnerabilities like SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and insecure cryptographic storage before code reaches the repository."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"git config --global core.hooksPath .githooks
# Inside .githooks/pre-commit:
echo "Running static analysis..."
semgrep --config auto"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 3: CI/CD Pipeline Security Automation"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Automated security gates must be embedded directly into the CI/CD pipeline. This includes SAST, Software Composition Analysis (SCA) for third-party dependencies, and Secret Detection."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: DevSecOps Pipeline
on: [push]
jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run Trivy Vulnerability Scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          scan-type: "fs"
          format: "sarif"
          output: "trivy-results.sarif""},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 4: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) and Container Scanning"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the application is built and deployed to a staging environment, DAST tools simulate real-world attacks against the running application. Additionally, container images must be scanned for OS-level vulnerabilities."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use OWASP ZAP for automated DAST scanning in staging environments."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce minimal base images (e.g., Alpine or Distroless) for Docker containers."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"By shifting security left into the early stages of the SDLC and automating checks within DevSecOps pipelines, organizations can significantly reduce remediation costs, minimize vulnerabilities in production, and foster a culture of shared security ownership."}]
